Can ML systems "think"? Are they "intelligent"? I honestly don't care. What matters is what capabilities & weaknesses they have, how we use them in practice, and what harms/benefits result. 

Definitional debates about what "real" intelligence is rarely help answer those Qs.

Govts already track aviation and cyber incidents. Given how general-purpose AI is, this kind of monitoring will be critical if our regulatory/policy environment is going to have any chance of keeping up with how these systems are working (and not working) in reality.

Then we wrap up with, of course, our policy recommendations. Funding AI safety research is in there, of course, but a more novel rec that I'm excited about is for governments to follow the lead of https://t.co/gFzAgVQf7y and start tracking what causes AI accidents in the wild.

We also point out risk factors that make failures especially likely, including competitive pressure (Boeing 737 MAX...), system complexity or speed, untrained/distracted users, and systems where one model is used in lots of places (e.g. Tesla autopilot in millions of cars).

We tell these stories in terms of three ways AI systems tend to fail - due to problems of robustness, specification, and assurance.

(big props to @v_maini and his team for this breakdown, and also for his super helpful review of this paper 🙏) https://t.co/dN7yoBrcSB

To do that, we came up with a dozen vignettes of fictional AI accidents, which draw heavily on things that have already happened (e.g. remember this? ⬇️) but imagine more widespread and slightly more capable AI.

Lossy: languages don't map perfectly onto each other. Different languages make it easier to express some concepts than others, or combine connotation & denotation in different ways. This makes it impossible to fully grasp what someone is saying if you only hear a translation. 4/5

Few-second delays might not sound like a big deal, but they make a huge difference to how a conversation feels. Turn-taking, clarification, nonverbal cues are all much more stilted. This matters less for pure exchange-of-facts conversations, but most communication isn't that. 3/5

Laggy: languages have different grammatical structures, so even with instant transcription & translation, the AI will often need to wait for the end of a phrase or sentence to know what has been said. This means the conversation is riddled with few-second delays. 2/5
